Lesson notes: learners keep notes beside each lesson, find them again and take them away

What this will achieve

Teachers working through a course can write notes beside each lesson without leaving the video. They can find any note again later and download their notes for a course to keep or share with colleagues.

Who it is for

Teachers and school staff learning at their own pace, often in short sessions between lessons, sometimes on a phone.

Done looks like

  • A learner types a note beside a lesson, leaves, comes back the next day and finds it exactly as they left it.
  • A learner searches "rubric" and sees every note that mentions it, each linked to its lesson.
  • A learner downloads all their notes for a course as one tidy document.
  • Notes work on a phone without covering the video.

Not in this phase

  • Sharing notes with other learners inside the site.
  • Notes on individual moments in a video.

How it will work, in plain English

Notes belong to one learner and one lesson and are saved as the learner types. They sit in a panel beside the lesson, chosen by mockup, so the video stays visible. Search looks only at the learner's own notes. Downloading builds one document from the saved notes, in lesson order. Each part is a separate module with a small front door, so search and download never reach into how notes are stored.

Architecture

Journey: writing a note during a lesson

The learner types beside the video; the note saves itself.

sequenceDiagram
  actor Learner
  Learner->>lesson-workspace: types in the notes panel
  lesson-workspace->>notes-store: saveNote(learner, lesson, text)
  notes-store-->>lesson-workspace: savedAt
  lesson-workspace-->>Learner: "Saved just now"
  • Stored: one row per learner and lesson in the existing learning database.
  • Checked: notes-store checks the learner owns the note on every read and write.
  • Leaves the system: nothing; notes are never sent to an AI model in this phase.
  • When it fails: the text stays in the panel and on the device, the panel says it could not save, and it tries again.

Journey: finding a note again

flowchart LR
  Search[Search box] --> notes-search --> notes-store
  notes-search --> Results[Matches with lesson and snippet]
  Results --> Lesson[Opens the lesson with the note]

UI decisions

Interactive mockups. Switch between the variants in each one; the approved variant is what units build against.

Where notes sit on the lesson screen

Notes below the video, or as a tab beside course contents. Try typing, switch states, and view at phone width.

Approved: B, side panel tab Decision D-001 Open full size

Decisions

D-001Where notes sit on the lesson screen2026-10-19

A tab in the side panel (variant B). Operator (example): "B — the video has to stay in view".

Question

Notes must be close to the video without hiding it, on desktop and on a phone.

Options

  1. Below the video. Simple, but learners scroll away from the video to type, and on a phone the notes sit far down the page.
  2. A tab in the side panel, beside course contents. The video stays in view while typing; on a phone the panel opens as a sheet under the video.

Decision

A tab in the side panel (variant B). Operator (example): "B — the video has to stay in view".

Why

Learners take notes while watching. Variant B keeps the video visible at every width and reuses the existing side panel, so there is no new layout to learn.

Consequences

lesson-workspace gains a Notes tab beside Contents. The phone layout needs a sheet that never covers the video.

D-002Notes save as the learner types2026-10-19

Save as they type, one second after the learner pauses.

Question

Should learners press Save, or should notes save themselves?

Options

  1. A Save button. Clear, but notes are lost when learners forget.
  2. Save as they type, a moment after they pause, with a quiet "Saved" line.

Decision

Save as they type, one second after the learner pauses.

Why

Sessions are short and often interrupted. A forgotten Save would lose exactly the notes learners care about.

Consequences

notes-store must accept frequent small saves, and the panel must show when a save failed.

Outcome

Each learner has one note per lesson that saves and loads through the notes-store front door, and nobody else can read or change it.

Done looks like

  • A saved note loads back exactly as typed, including line breaks — proved by src/notes/store/save.test.ts
  • Another learner's request for the note is refused — proved by src/notes/store/access.test.ts
  • Rapid saves keep the newest text — proved by src/notes/store/save.test.ts

Not in scope

  • The notes panel on screen (WU-0002).
  • Search and export.

Approach

Add a notes table keyed by learner and lesson, through a generated migration. notes-store exposes saveNote, loadNote and listNotes; every call checks the learner against the session. Saves are last-write-wins on a saved-at time.
